inputSnapshot.objective: Elite-style single-player space trading and combat game with a rich browser frontend played in Google Chrome. A local Node.js server serves the game; the player opens http://localhost:<port> in Chrome and plays immediately (npm install && npm start, no manual build steps). The frontend is a first-class acceptance subject: a beautiful single-page canvas/WebGL application with a parallax starfield, hyperspace jump effect, station docking screen, ship HUD (shields, fuel, cargo, credits), commodity market screen with dynamic prices, and arcade laser combat with visual effects. Core gameplay loop: start docked at a station with 100 credits and a small cargo hold; buy low / sell high across a galaxy of at least 8 named systems with per-system price variation; hyperspace jumps consume fuel and carry pirate-encounter risk; win ship-to-ship combat (player lasers vs enemy AI) or flee; spend profits on ship upgrades (cargo capacity, laser, shields, fuel tank); progress toward the Elite rating tracked by profit and combat kills; save/load the game state. Non-functional: 60fps target on a 2020 laptop in Chrome, no external CDN dependencies (fully offline), English UI. Testing: unit tests for market pricing, jump/fuel math, combat resolution and save/load; a browser smoke test that loads the page and asserts the canvas renders; the server must expose /healthz.

assumptions: Node.js is available on the development machine
Chrome is the target browser and will be used for testing
The player has basic familiarity with space trading games
A 2020 laptop is a reasonable minimum hardware target for 60fps
WebSocket or similar real-time communication is not required (single-player)
Local filesystem access for save/load is acceptable
proposalPayload.candidate_scope: The minimum useful product scope includes: a Node.js server that serves a single HTML/JS frontend; a canvas/WebGL rendering system with parallax starfield; at least 8 named star systems with stations; a commodity market with dynamic per-system pricing; hyperspace jump mechanics with fuel consumption and pirate encounter probability; ship-to-ship combat with player lasers vs enemy AI; ship upgrades (cargo capacity, laser, shields, fuel tank); save/load game state functionality; unit tests for core mechanics; a browser smoke test; and a /healthz endpoint on the server.
